These are my estimates from prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 structure. I did not run any benchmark data.

Setting an edge to none hurts more when the remaining paths are few, so it is more damaging when the cell is already sparse. The same logic makes a conv or skip edit more valuable when alternative paths are missing.

The edit-specific reasoning is brief and uncertain, and the numbers are mostly low, since consistency across all three datasets with a meaningful margin is a demanding bar.
